issues.description: Forward-reference 'FrameProcessor' annotation on dataclass field has no matching TYPE_CHECKING import.
issues.detail: The new `service: "FrameProcessor"` field in frames.py uses a string annotation but no `FrameProcessor` import exists, even under TYPE_CHECKING. `typing.get_type_hints()` will raise NameError, IDEs cannot resolve it, and dataclass introspection sees a string. Add a TYPE_CHECKING import or widen the annotation.

issues.description: Equality check on FrameProcessor instances should be identity (`is`), not `==`.
issues.detail: The guard `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on default `__eq__` falling back to identity. The actual invariant is "same processor instance." Use `is` to state intent explicitly and survive any future override that gives FrameProcessor value equality. One-character fix removing a class of latent bug.

issues.description: Inactive-service branch silently leaks the request frame downstream with no test or documentation.
issues.detail: Old code suppressed every `RequestMetadataFrame`; new code only suppresses when `frame.service == active_service`. A frame targeting an inactive service now escapes past the switcher. Either forbid non-active targets explicitly, document the invariant that upstream filters block them, or handle both branches as named cases with tests.

issues.description: Embedding a live FrameProcessor reference in the frame complects value with identity and splits routing logic.
issues.detail: A control frame should be a value, but `service: FrameProcessor` carries a mutable processor reference. The frame becomes unserializable/unloggable, and the "who consumes this" decision is now split between the switcher's equality check and every service that re-pushes the frame. A stable service id (data) plus a single consume rule would be simpler.

issues.description: Tests do not assert that `frame.service` points at the intended target processor.
issues.detail: The new test checks `len(request_frames) == 1` but never verifies `request_frames[0].service is self.service2`. Since targeting a specific service is the whole point of this patch, a regression that sets `service=` to the wrong processor would pass green. Add the identity assertion and cover the inactive-target branch.

issues.description: Frame ordering change in STTService is undocumented and untested.
issues.detail: STTService now emits `_push_stt_metadata()` then forwards the `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` rather than swallowing it. Downstream consumers observe a new ordering `[STTMetadataFrame, ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame]` with no comment stating the invariant and no test pinning order. Add a one-line invariant comment and an ordering assertion.

synthesis.summary: The rename and targeted-suppression refactor is small and readable, but it rests on unstated invariants and a questionable data shape. The panel agrees on three P1 issues: the new `service` dataclass field has a broken forward-reference annotation, equality should be identity, and the inactive-service branch now silently leaks the request frame downstream without documentation or tests. Hickey additionally flags that embedding a live FrameProcessor reference in a control frame complects value with identity and splits routing logic across the switcher and every service. Two P2 cleanups round it out: tests should assert the target processor identity, and the new STT frame ordering deserves a comment and a test. NEEDS-WORK, not a refuse.
